f: Steve asked if it was lots of small ones or one big one. Ricky: "lots of little small ones yeah."
ex: Um. I’d have probably been wearing the shirt my mum got me from Tescos, which was uh, which was again a Brutus shirt, and, uh, it had women in bikinis eating bananas.
What, lots of small ones? Or just one big one?
Yeah yeah yeah, lots of little small ones yeah, so uh, y’know, uh, uhhhh, so that was that.

q: Why did Karl end up with juice running down his face just before Rockbusters?
a: Ricky squashed a juicy pear on his head for a William Tell stunt
x: Steve squirted an orange at him for sulking
Ricky poured his tea over him as a wake-up call
He bit into a peach while pressing the buttons
f: Karl's head was so round that Ricky flattened the pear first, not realising it was a juicy one. He insisted the pear was to blame.
ex: Right, what were you trying to put on me head?

I was trying to put a pear, on your head to knock it off with a ball, like William Tell. But, it was- d- your, because your head is so round, and the pear was round, I tried to flatten it a little bit, and I didn't know it was a juicy pear.
So, I thought it'd be like a, just, crush it a little bit, and then he went mental because he had juice rubbin- running down his face!
Why's it my fault, the pear's a faulty f- pear!
Get proper fruit in here! It worked with the apple!

q: Someone called Sophie sent Ricky something from the Czech Republic. What was it?
a: The lid of a cream cheese with the brand name Gervais
x: A sausage with the brand name Merchant
f: Sophie wrote "I realize you're not Graham Norton". Ricky decided it must be his ancestors: "cheese is in my blood. Quite literally."
ex: No, but someone sent me- Sophie, here, sent me something and she said, “I realize you’re not Graham Norton, but I had to send you this” and she sent me the top of a little cream cheesy thing and it’s-it’s, the brand name is Gervais.
How odd that is! They’ve named a cheese after you.
I think it’s a big French company and this is from the Czech Republic. It’s all over Europe and so--
That would be a dream come true, wouldn’t it, if they named a cheese after you?
No, I think it’s, I think it’s, uh, probably, you know, ancestors and so I’ve- cheese is in my blood.

q: In Ricky's theory of how sumo began, a fat bloke took on a skinny Kung Fu expert. What rule did the fat bloke insist on?
a: No punching, just leaning against each other
f: The skinny bloke saw through it straight away: "Well, you're bound to win!"
ex: I reckon it was a fat bloke who was picking on a little skinny bloke and the skinny bloke knew King Fu and Jujitsu. Goes, “Right, let’s fight.” And the fat one, “There’s no punching.”
He goes, “What do you mean?” “It’s just leaning against each other.”
And the other one, “Well, you’re bound to win!” And then, “Right, I’ve won.” “Okay.” And that’s how it started and then the fat bloke--

q: Ricky claimed he beat Karl at penalties when they played football in his garden. What was the score?
a: Five-two
f: Ricky also claimed a 10-4 win "on a knockout" and said Karl always makes an excuse: "No, start again."
ex: We had a little- well. I did.

No, you were rubbish. I beat you in penalties, um, five-two and then I beat you on, uh, a knockout, I think, ten-four and then he always makes an excuse. He goes, “No, start again. We didn’t say--” He- I’m cracking up.
